concepts.heading: Rethinking What Desire "Should" Look Like
concepts.alt: A guide watching a small lightning bolt fizzle out while a warm glowing ember grows in her hands
concepts.plain: Wanting sex does not always strike out of the blue. That is only one way it works.

concepts.heading: Dr. Rosemary Basson's Responsive Desire Model
concepts.plain: For many people, wanting comes after things start to feel good, not before.

concepts.heading: Spontaneous vs. Responsive Desire
concepts.alt: He holds a lightning bolt, she holds a slowly warming candle, both smiling
concepts.plain: Some people feel desire first. Others feel it once things get going. Both are normal.

concepts.heading: The Full Spectrum of Desire
concepts.alt: A guide standing beside a long dial that runs from low to high, pointing to the middle
concepts.plain: People want sex in very different amounts and ways. All of it is normal.

concepts.heading: A Trauma-Informed Perspective
concepts.plain: If you feel shame about how your desire works, nothing is wrong with you.

checks.prompt: Dana rarely feels desire out of nowhere, but it builds once things feel warm and connected. What kind of desire is this?
checks.explanation: Responsive desire. Responsive desire shows up in response to things like touch, closeness or the right setting, and the lesson calls it equally normal.

checks.prompt: How does the lesson describe desire?
checks.explanation: As a wide spectrum. Desire exists on a wide spectrum. Some people experience strong spontaneous desire throughout their lives.

9937453f-0d6e-4fb6-bca2-39cadcbe8fe0.takeaway: Desire that shows up after things get going is just as normal as desire that shows up first.

concepts.heading: Your Sexual Response Has Two Systems
concepts.alt: A guide sitting in a small cartoon car with one foot hovering over two pedals
concepts.plain: Think of a car: you have a gas pedal for turn-ons and a brake for turn-offs.

concepts.heading: The Sexual Excitation System (Accelerators)
concepts.alt: A guide pressing a green accelerator pedal, small hearts sparking around it
concepts.plain: The gas pedal is everything that turns you on.

concepts.heading: The Sexual Inhibition System (Brakes)
concepts.alt: A guide pressing a red brake pedal, a stop sign beside her
concepts.plain: The brake is everything that turns you off, like stress or worry.

concepts.heading: Why "Just Relax" Doesn't Work
concepts.alt: A guide pushing a small car from behind while its red brake light stays on
concepts.plain: "Just relax" fails because the fix is taking your foot off the brake, not pushing the gas.

concepts.heading: Sensitive Brakes Are Not Dysfunction
concepts.plain: Some people have touchy brakes. That is how they are built, not a problem.

concepts.heading: Context Is Everything
concepts.alt: A guide arranging a cosy corner with a soft lamp, a plant and a blanket
concepts.plain: Where you are, how you feel and who you are with change everything.

checks.prompt: Stress, distraction and self-consciousness all press on which system?
checks.explanation: The brakes (inhibition). Your Sexual Inhibition System (SIS) is everything that reduces or suppresses your sexual response.

checks.prompt: Why does "just relax" or "try harder" rarely help?
checks.explanation: The brakes are still on. The dual control model explains why: trying harder presses the accelerator while the brakes stay on.

b5984aa9-678f-47d3-8f91-3d71a1f83eef.takeaway: Desire needs more gas and less brake. Easing what holds you back often helps most.

concepts.heading: Desire Discrepancy Is Normal
concepts.alt: Two guides holding batteries with different charge levels, smiling at each other
concepts.plain: Partners almost never want sex the exact same amount. That is normal.

concepts.heading: New Relationship Energy (NRE)
concepts.alt: A guide floating among fizzing sparkles and hearts
concepts.plain: New love brings a rush of desire. It fades, and that is normal too.

concepts.heading: Navigating Desire Differences
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting facing each other with a question mark and a magnifying glass between them
concepts.plain: Swap blame for curiosity. Ask what helps instead of who is wrong.

concepts.heading: Basson's Model in Your Relationships
concepts.plain: You may feel desire differently with different partners. That is okay.

concepts.heading: Communication Without Pressure
concepts.alt: Two guides talking on a sofa with relaxed open hands, a small dove above them
concepts.plain: Talk about desire in a way that never makes someone feel they owe you.

checks.prompt: Partners want sex at different rates. What shift does the lesson recommend?
checks.explanation: From blame to curiosity. When partners have different desire patterns, the key is to move from blame to curiosity.

checks.prompt: Partners wanting sex at different times or amounts is…
options: A sign the relationship is failing
One of the most common concerns
checks.explanation: One of the most common concerns. One of the most common concerns people bring to therapists and relationship discussions is desire discrepancy — when partners want sex at different frequencies or in different ways.

014cae3a-3a48-465e-9947-12c9956244e6.takeaway: Partners rarely want the same amount of sex. Get curious instead of blaming.

concepts.heading: Desire Is a Garden, Not a Light Switch
concepts.alt: A guide watering a small garden of heart-shaped flowers, a crossed-out light switch beside her
concepts.plain: Desire is like a garden. You tend it. It is not a switch you flip.

concepts.heading: Mindfulness and Embodiment
concepts.alt: Eyes closed with a hand on his chest, breathing slowly, small leaves floating by
concepts.plain: Get out of your head and notice what your body feels.

concepts.heading: The Role of Context
concepts.plain: Set up the things that help, like rest, time and feeling safe.

concepts.heading: Scheduling Intimacy
concepts.alt: Two guides marking a heart on a shared wall calendar together
concepts.plain: Planning time for closeness is not unromantic. It shows it matters.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Professional Support
concepts.plain: If desire changes a lot and it worries you, a professional can help.

concepts.heading: Desire Is Connection
concepts.plain: At heart, desire is about feeling connected to yourself and to others.

checks.prompt: The lesson says desire is more like a garden than a…
checks.explanation: Light switch. One of the most liberating shifts in understanding desire is moving from thinking of it as something that either happens or doesn't — like a light switch — to understanding it as something you can cultivate, like a garden.

checks.prompt: Why do many people resist scheduling intimacy?
checks.explanation: It feels "unromantic". Many people resist the idea of scheduling intimacy because it feels "unromantic."

e377b076-3a3f-453c-acad-6238032b676a.takeaway: Desire grows when you tend it: rest, safety, time and attention.
